title: Erectile dysfunction (ED)
subject: urology
setting: Primary care, urology or andrology outpatient
summary: Treat ED as a marker of cardiovascular disease: take a medical and sexual history, check glucose, lipids and morning testosterone, stratify cardiac risk (Princeton IV), modify risk factors, and use a PDE5 inhibitor first line unless the man takes nitrates, nicorandil or riociguat.

sections.title: Recognise
items: ED: persistent inability to attain and maintain an erection sufficient for satisfactory sexual performance. Most cases are mixed organic and psychogenic.
ED raises the risk of cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation and death, and can be an early sign of coronary or peripheral vascular disease.
Clues to a mainly psychogenic cause: sudden onset, situational ED, preserved morning or nocturnal erections. Mainly organic: gradual onset, loss of nocturnal erections, vascular risk factors.

Ask about medicines (antihypertensives, antidepressants, antipsychotics, antiandrogens, 5-ARIs), alcohol, smoking, recreational drugs, pelvic surgery or radiotherapy, trauma, diabetes, and other sexual problems (low desire, premature ejaculation, penile curvature).

sections.title: Assessment
items: Use a validated questionnaire (for example the IIEF) to grade ED and measure response.

Focused examination: genitals (Peyronie plaque, small testes), signs of hypogonadism, BP and heart rate (if not measured in the last 3 to 6 months), BMI or waist, peripheral pulses, prostate if urinary symptoms, and neurological status.

Tests: fasting glucose or HbA1c and lipid profile (if not done in the last 12 months) and a morning total testosterone. Repeat a low testosterone at least once; 12 nmol/L (3.5 ng/mL) is the EAU threshold for considering treatment.

Specialist tests (penile duplex ultrasound, nocturnal tumescence testing, endocrine or psychosexual assessment) for primary ED, young men after pelvic or perineal trauma, penile deformity, complex psychiatric or endocrine disease, or medicolegal reasons.

sections.title: Cardiovascular risk before treatment (Princeton IV)
items: No known cardiovascular disease: calculate 10-year ASCVD risk. With a suspected vasculogenic cause and intermediate risk, coronary artery calcium scoring can guide statin and aspirin decisions (Princeton IV, adopted by EAU).

Known cardiovascular disease or cardiac symptoms: assess exercise tolerance. Low risk: treat ED. Intermediate or indeterminate risk: exercise stress test before treatment. High risk: refer to cardiology and defer sexual activity until stable.

High-risk features: unstable or refractory angina, recent myocardial infarction, uncontrolled arrhythmia or hypertension, advanced heart failure, significant valve disease (especially aortic stenosis) or hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.
On nitrates or riociguat: PDE5 inhibitors are contraindicated; consider whether nitrates can be stopped, otherwise use non-PDE5 options.

sections.title: Treatment
items: Start lifestyle and risk factor changes (weight loss, exercise, stopping smoking, control of glucose, BP and lipids) before or alongside ED treatment; change culprit drugs where possible.

PDE5 inhibitors are first line. Explain they need sexual stimulation and correct timing; incorrect use is the main cause of apparent failure, so give an adequate trial at the right dose before switching.

Choose by pattern: sildenafil (effect from 30 to 60 minutes, up to 12 hours), vardenafil (from about 30 minutes), avanafil (15 to 30 minutes), tadalafil on demand (from 30 minutes, up to 36 hours) or tadalafil 5 mg daily (also treats LUTS).
Offer psychosexual therapy or CBT, ideally including the partner, combined with medical treatment when psychological factors contribute.

Alternatives or second line: intracavernous alprostadil 5 to 40 micrograms (in-office training first), intraurethral or topical alprostadil, vacuum erection device (not with bleeding disorders or anticoagulants), low-intensity shockwave therapy for mild vasculogenic ED.
Penile prosthesis if other treatments fail or by preference. Testosterone therapy for confirmed hypogonadism with symptoms, which may improve response to PDE5 inhibitors.

sections.title: PDE5 inhibitor safety
items: Absolutely contraindicated with any organic nitrate or nitric oxide donor (GTN, isosorbide, amyl nitrite poppers) and with nicorandil or riociguat.
If a man on a PDE5 inhibitor develops chest pain, do not give nitrates within 24 hours of sildenafil or vardenafil, or 48 hours of tadalafil; use other anti-anginal treatment.
Alpha-blockers and other antihypertensives cause small additive BP falls; EAU finds no need to avoid the combination, but start low if he is prone to postural hypotension.
Use lower starting doses in severe renal or hepatic impairment and with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example ritonavir, clarithromycin, ketoconazole).
Advise urgent care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, and stopping the drug and seeking review for sudden loss of vision or hearing.

sections.title: Referral
items: Urology or andrology: failure of PDE5 inhibitors despite correct use, penile deformity, primary ED, young men after trauma, candidates for injections or prosthesis.
Endocrinology: low testosterone with suspected pituitary cause, raised prolactin or other endocrine disease.
Cardiology: intermediate or high cardiac risk. Psychosexual services: predominantly psychogenic ED or relationship factors.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Prescribing a PDE5 inhibitor without asking about nitrates, nicorandil or recreational poppers.
Treating the erection and missing diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia or coronary disease.
Labelling PDE5 inhibitor failure after one or two attempts or after incorrect use (for example sildenafil after a heavy fatty meal, or without stimulation).
Starting testosterone without a confirmed low morning level on repeat testing.
Missing over-the-counter herbal sexual enhancers, which may contain undeclared PDE5 inhibitors.

drugs.name: Sildenafil
drugs.dose: 50 mg orally about 1 hour before sex (range 25 to 100 mg), no more than once daily
drugs.notes: Start 25 mg with severe renal or hepatic impairment or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Absorption slowed by fatty meals. Contraindicated with nitrates.

drugs.name: Tadalafil (on demand)
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally at least 30 minutes before sex, increased to 20 mg if needed, no more than once daily
drugs.notes: Effective up to 36 hours. No nitrates for 48 hours after a dose.

drugs.name: Tadalafil (daily)
drugs.notes: For frequent sexual activity or coexisting LUTS.

drugs.name: Vardenafil
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally 25 to 60 minutes before sex (range 5 to 20 mg), no more than once daily

drugs.name: Avanafil
drugs.dose: 100 mg orally 15 to 30 minutes before sex (range 50 to 200 mg), no more than once daily

drugs.name: Alprostadil (intracavernous)
drugs.dose: 5 to 40 micrograms by intracavernous injection, titrated from a low dose under supervision
drugs.notes: Second line or when PDE5 inhibitors are contraindicated. Penile pain; priapism risk about 1%.

drugs.name: Alprostadil (intraurethral)
drugs.dose: Start 500 micrograms, increase to 1000 micrograms if needed
